title: Alice & Bob Demonstrates GPU Decoding for LDPC-Cat Codes via NVIDIA NVQLink - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Alice & Bob showed proof-of-concept GPU decoding of its LDPC-cat error-correction architecture over NVIDIA NVQLink, streaming synthetic data from Quantum Machines OPX1000 hardware with microsecond-scale roundtrips. The test was offline with synthetic data, not real-time QPU feedback.

insights.claim: Alice & Bob presented proof-of-concept results decoding its LDPC-cat quantum error correction architecture on NVIDIA GPUs using the low-latency NVQLink architecture.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Adds Alice & Bob to the set of QEC players integrating with NVIDIA's quantum-GPU interconnect.

insights.claim: The test transferred synthetic measurement data from Quantum Machines' OPX1000 control hardware to GPUs through the Open Acceleration Stack, establishing microsecond-scale roundtrip communication between quantum control systems and classical GPU supercomputers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Microsecond roundtrip latency is the key number for real-time decoding; a third-party control vendor (Quantum Machines) is part of the stack.

insights.claim: NVQLink is described as a high-throughput, tight-coupling interface designed to accelerate real-time error-correction decoding, calibration, and hybrid quantum-classical workloads.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Positions NVIDIA as the standard interconnect between QPUs and GPU compute.

insights.claim: The demonstration used synthetic data off-line rather than real-time QPU feedback, but validates parallel syndrome decoding efficiency across GPU clusters.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This is an interface and throughput proof, not an end-to-end real-time QEC result; discount accordingly.
insights.quote: synthetic data off-line rather than real-time QPU feedback

insights.claim: NVIDIA GPU clusters decode multiple syndrome streams in parallel so that decoding throughput can scale alongside QPU size.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Parallel decoding scaling is the property needed as qubit counts grow.

insights.claim: Alice & Bob's architecture combines cat qubits, which exponentially suppress physical bit-flip errors through continuous non-linear dissipation, with 2D low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware-level bit-flip protection reduces the burden on the code, the basis of the claimed overhead advantage.

insights.claim: The LDPC-cat architecture enables 100 logical qubits on a 758 cat-qubit chip with logical error rates below 10^-8 per cycle.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A roughly 7.6 physical-to-logical ratio would be very low overhead if achieved; it is an architectural figure, not an experimental result in this article.

insights.claim: The work builds on Alice & Bob's decoupled AI control topologies to resolve microsecond latencies for cat qubits and on its partnership with Bull to integrate cat qubit processors into HPC supercomputing infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Indicates a go-to-market through supercomputing centers rather than standalone systems.
